hello.note: Use it until the evening, then bonsoir (bohn-SWAHR). Greet shop and restaurant staff with it as you walk in

good-morning.note: French has no separate good morning: bonjour covers the whole day until the evening

good-night.note: Only at bedtime or when parting late. To greet someone in the evening, say bonsoir (bohn-SWAHR)

goodbye.note: Bonne journée (bun zhoor-NAY) is a friendly goodbye meaning have a good day

thank-you.note: Merci beaucoup (boh-KOO) means thank you very much

no.note: The n is nasal and barely sounded

excuse-me.note: Pardon (par-DOHN) also works to get past someone or say sorry

my-name.note: Literally "I call myself". The audio uses Peter as the example name

dont-understand.note: In fast speech the ne disappears: je comprends pas

speak-english.note: Say bonjour first: people are far more willing to switch to English

one.note: A nasal vowel. Before a feminine noun it is une (ewn)

five.note: Nasal vowel; the q is pronounced here

how-much.note: C'est combien ? (seh kohm-BYAN) is the casual version

would-like.note: The polite way to order. Je voudrais un café = I'd like a coffee. The audio uses un café as the example

i-want.note: Blunt in French; je voudrais is politer. The audio uses ça (this) as the example

do-you-have.note: Put the item in the gap. The audio uses de l'eau (water) as the example

just-looking.note: Staff may ask Je peux vous aider ? (can I help you?)

ill-take-it.note: For a feminine item say je la prends

discount.note: Haggling is rare in France; try only at flea markets

bill.note: In France the bill only comes when you ask for it

checkout-time.text: À quelle heure faut-il libérer la chambre ?
checkout-time.say: ah kehl UHR foh-teel lee-bay-RAY lah SHAHM-bruh
checkout-time.note: Literally "at what time must the room be vacated?"

wifi.text: Quel est le mot de passe du wifi ?
wifi.say: kehl eh luh moh duh PAHSS dew wee-FEE

toilet.note: "Où est …?" (oo eh) means "where is …?" for anything singular

bus.note: A long-distance coach is un autocar (oh-toh-KAR)

train-station.note: Also used in names: Gare du Nord

which-train.note: Swap in any city; the audio uses Hanoï (ah-NOY) as the example

two-tickets.note: The audio uses Hanoï as the example city
two-tickets.spoken: Puis-je acheter deux billets pour Hanoï ?

trip-length.text: Combien de temps dure le trajet pour... ?
trip-length.say: kohm-BYAN duh tahn dewr luh trah-ZHEH poor ...
trip-length.note: The audio uses Hanoï as the example city
trip-length.spoken: Combien de temps dure le trajet pour Hanoï ?

delicious.note: C'est un régal (seh tuhn ray-GAL) is a bigger compliment

allergic.note: Add the food: aux fruits de mer (seafood), aux noix (nuts), aux œufs (eggs). The audio uses fruits de mer as the example
allergic.spoken: Je suis allergique aux fruits de mer

love-dish.note: Adorer is stronger than aimer, and both work for food

what-called.note: Point at the dish or item

table-for-two.text: Une table pour deux, s'il vous plaît
table-for-two.say: ewn TAH-bluh poor DUH seel voo PLEH
table-for-two.note: For more people use trois (3) or quatre (4) instead of deux

menu.text: Puis-je avoir la carte, s'il vous plaît ?
menu.say: pwee-zhuh ah-VWAHR lah KART seel voo PLEH
menu.note: La carte is the menu list; le menu is a fixed-price meal

beer.text: Une bouteille de bière, s'il vous plaît
beer.say: ewn boo-TAY duh bee-AIR seel voo PLEH
beer.note: Un demi (uhn duh-MEE) is a small draught beer, the most common order

coffee.note: It is a small black espresso. Un café crème (krem) has milk

water.note: Une carafe d'eau (ewn kah-RAF DOH) is free tap water, and you can ask for it in restaurants

cheers.note: Literally "health". À votre santé (ah VOH-truh) is the polite version

help.note: Shout it. The police are la police (lah poh-LEES)
